tldr: Midday batch, Aug 17: The big one — Stripe is closing in on a $7B+ deal to buy OpenRouter, a major consolidation play at the AI-infrastructure layer that would put one of the biggest model gateways inside a payments giant. Separately, two pieces land on the knowledge-vs-reasoning trade: an essay argues labs are deliberately shrinking world knowledge to buy reasoning skill (small models now hallucinate ~80% of facts), while top mathematicians tell The Decoder LLMs are strong calculators but poor creative thinkers. Qwen3.8 keeps dominating local-model talk: a custom engine hits 82 tps single-request on a 3090 with 195K context, and Simon Willison calls the 27B the most fun local model in ages — though it defaults to wildly overthinking. Most of the X-account news (DeepSeek V4-Pro, Qwen3.8 open weights, Hermes Agent updates, Anthropic Risk Report) was already covered in this morning's push.

articles.title: Stripe Clinches Over $7B Deal to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter

articles.title: Models Are Getting Dumber on Purpose
articles.summary: Essay argues labs deliberately trade world knowledge for reasoning: small models ace math/code but hallucinate ~80% of factual recall.

articles.summary: Leading mathematicians say LLMs excel at calculation but fall short on creative, open-ended math thinking.

articles.title: Qwen3.8-27B on RTX 3090 — 82 tps Single Request, Up to 672 tps Peak

articles.title: Simon Willison: Qwen 3.8 27B Is Excellent, But Defaults to Wildly Overthinking
articles.summary: Simon Willison calls Qwen3.8 27B the most fun local model in a long time — excellent quality, but it defaults to overthinking even simple requests.
